title: fleet-utilization-playbook-workload-tiering-sheet
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet captures a tactical playbook for mapping LLM workload tiers to an optimized GPU fleet mix by region, with quick heuristics to estimate GPU-hour burn and $/1M tokens. It is intended for infra planners and cost-ops when sizing new regions or negotiating reserved commitments.

High-level approach:
1) Classify request surface into workload tiers (interactive, async-low-priority, batch, embeddings-heavy).
2) For each tier, estimate request mix, average sequence length, and p50/p95 latency targets to translate into tokens/sec and effective GPU throughput.
3) Convert throughput into GPU-hour requirement using kernel-level utilization factors and batching assumptions.
4) Apply regional price bands and reserve/spot mix to compute $/1M tokens and sensitivity to utilization.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Model families: small-enc (7B equiv), med-decoder (30B equiv), large-decoder (70B equiv), embeddings-large (19B embedding model).
- Effective tokens-per-second when served on a single H100-80GB equiv instance (continuous batching, avg batch 8):
  - small-enc: 1,500 tokens/sec
  - med-decoder: 450 tokens/sec
  - large-decoder: 160 tokens/sec
  - embeddings-large: 2,800 tokens/sec
- Average request composition by product (sample): chat 42%, single-turn generation 28%, embeddings 22%, rerank/others 8%.
- Baseline GPU efficiency factors (include KV cache benefits for multi-turn):
  - warm-cached interactive: 0.75 effective utilization multiplier
  - cold-starts and long-context: 0.55 multiplier
- Target baseline utilization for reserved pool: 0.65 (planning), burst pool can be 0.25/spot-heavy.

Workload tier mapping (editable table):
Tier | Typical model | Avg seq len | Req mix% | tokens/sec per-request | Notes
Interactive (low-latency) | med-decoder | 120 | 42% | 250 | p95 latency SLO tight -> prefix cache enabled
Async (best-effort) | large-decoder | 600 | 18% | 1,200 | batched aggressively, higher tail latency tolerated
Embeddings | embeddings-large | 256 | 22% | 800 | highly parallel, vectorization wins
Batch jobs | small-enc / med-decoder | 1,200 | 12% | 3,600 | scheduled nightly, can use spot/ephemeral pool
Rerank/QA | small-enc | 64 | 6% | 120 | often runs as pipeline stage

Example conversion to GPU-hours (method):
1) Compute tokens/sec demand = active_qps * avg_tokens_per_request.
2) Total tokens/sec per model family -> divide by model tokens/sec capacity above -> concurrent GPUs required.
3) GPU-hours/day = concurrent_gpus * 24.
4) Adjust for utilization: planned_gpu_hours = gpu_hours/day / target_utilization.

Quick worked example (single region planning, mixed product traffic):
- Peak active QPS (global routed to this region after routing policy): 1,800 active requests.
- Using request mix and avg seq lengths from above, compute tokens/sec demand (simplified):
  - Interactive: 1,800 * 0.42 * 120 tokens = 90,720 tokens/s
  - Async: 1,800 * 0.18 * 600 tokens = 194,400 tokens/s
  - Embeddings: 1,800 * 0.22 * 256 tokens = 101,376 tokens/s
  - Batch: 1,800 * 0.12 * 1,200 tokens = 259,200 tokens/s
  - Rerank: 1,800 * 0.06 * 64 tokens = 6,912 tokens/s
  - Total tokens/s = 652,608 tokens/s
- Map to GPU capacity (using per-GPU tokens/sec capacity mix; we choose a heterogeneous mix with H100 equiv for decoders and A100 equiv for embeddings):
  - Assume combined average tokens/sec per GPU weighted mix = 1,200 tokens/sec (blended).
  - Concurrent GPUs = 652,608 / 1,200 = 544 GPUs (rounded up).
  - GPU-hours/day = 544 * 24 = 13,056 GPU-hours/day.
  - Adjust for utilization target 0.65 -> planned GPU-hours/day = 13,056 / 0.65 = 20,085 GPU-hours/day (capacity to reserve).

Per-region unit economics (sample price bands and $/1M tokens outputs)
Price assumptions (effective blended cost to Redwood for reserved+spot mix; editable per-region):
  - us-west (primary): $2.50 / GPU-hour (blended)
  - us-east (primary): $2.40 / GPU-hour
  - eu-west: $3.10 / GPU-hour
  - ap-southeast: $4.20 / GPU-hour
  - ap-south: $3.60 / GPU-hour

Compute $/1M tokens (worked):
- Use planned GPU-hours/day from example (20,085 GPU-hrs/day) and total tokens/sec -> tokens/day = 652,608 * 86,400 = 56,375,731,200 tokens/day (~56.4B).
- tokens per day per 1M = 56,375.73 units of 1M tokens.
- cost/day (us-west) = 20,085 * $2.50 = $50,212.50.
- $ / 1M tokens (us-west) = 50,212.50 / 56,375.73 = $0.89 per 1M tokens.
- Quick regional examples (using same demand but regional price):
  - us-east: cost/day = 20,085 * 2.40 = $48,204 -> $0.85 / 1M tokens
  - eu-west: cost/day = 20,085 * 3.10 = $62,263.50 -> $1.10 / 1M tokens
  - ap-southeast: cost/day = 20,085 * 4.20 = $84,357 -> $1.50 / 1M tokens
  - ap-south: cost/day = 20,085 * 3.60 = $72,306 -> $1.28 / 1M tokens

Sensitivity notes:
- If average batching increases from 8 to 12 for decoder workloads, blended tokens/sec per GPU increases ~30% leading to ~$ / 1M drop of ~23% (non-linear due to utilization floor).
- Moving 30% of reserved capacity to spot (savings band ~35% on GPU-hour) reduces blended cost by ~10% overall but increases outage risk for burst windows.
- Increasing target utilization from 0.65 -> 0.75 reduces capacity reserve by ~13% (directly reduces $/1M). Operational burden: higher autoscaler churn and risk to p95.

Recommended fleet strategy (playbook):
- Baseline reserved pool sized for 72-hour rolling peak at 0.65 utilization in primary regions (us-west/us-east).
- Maintain a warm burst pool (10–15% of baseline) composed primarily of spot/ephemeral instances with preemption-aware job routing for async/batch workloads.
- Embeddings-heavy capacity should preferentially use A100-class instances deployed in a separate autoscale group to enable cheaper vectorization kernels and lower memory pressure.
- Canary regions: when launching a new region, start with 15% of projected baseline as reserved and route 5–10% of traffic for canary validation.

Operational play: scaling policies and routing knobs
- Route by SLO and cost: interactive requests prefer primary regions and reserved capacity; embeddings and batch prefer cheapest region with acceptable latency.
- Fallback policy: on reserved saturation, failover to burst pool with degraded SLO for non-interactive tiers only.
- Autoscaler configs (starter): target_cpu = high threshold, target_gpu_util = 0.60 (scale up), grace_period = 60s for interactive, 300s for batch pools.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Validate blended tokens/sec per-GPU for our latest compiled kernels (ENG-1838 perf PR).
- Confirm reserved pricing + committed discount tiers with procurement for new EU/AP reservations (finance action: request quotes).
- Add real telemetry mapping: translate token accounting from prod logs to request mix by region (owner: Lina).

Action items:
- Rafiq: run a 7-day simulation in dev env with current traffic replay to validate GPU-hour/day conversion (due 2025-02-28).
- Aditya: surface spot preemption traces to estimate realistic availability windows (due 2025-03-07).
- Maya: prepare a one-pager for finance showing $/1M by region under 3 reserve/spot mixes (conservative/balanced/aggressive) (due 2025-03-05).

Notes (context):
- This sheet intentionally uses a blended-per-GPU abstraction to keep initial planning simple. Follow-up should replace blended factors with model-family-specific capacity curves once kernel perf matrix from applied-ml is finalized.
- Keep this doc as the canonical working sheet for near-term capacity discussions; final numbers will live in the central fleet-sizing sheet once validated.

Revision log:
- 2025-01-10 Maya: initial draft and baseline assumptions
- 2025-02-22 Maya: added worked example and per-region unit-econ quick table
